title: $\mathcal{O}_X(D)$ agrees with the divisor module of file 06
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $C$ a smooth connected curve over $k$ and $D=\sum_{i=1}^m n_i[P_i]$ a divisor of $C$ which is an effective Cartier divisor (so the coefficients are nonnegative). Then the module $\mathcal{O}_C(D)$ of [def-sc-divisor] (a sub-$\mathcal{O}_C$-module of the constant sheaf $k(C)$) and the module $\mathcal{O}_C(D)$ of [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] are canonically isomorphic.

proof.text: Set E(P)=D(P).toNat. Effectiveness identifies the integer cast of E with D, and Finsupp.prod_mapRange_index identifies Divisor.idealSheaf E with the product in the conclusion. Smoothness and connectedness give regularity and integrality; finite type gives Noetherianity, and the curve dimension gives SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1. By [lem-sc-point-cartier], the ideal product is invertible. Use its proved source API in Curve.DivisorIdealSheaf: isInvertible_idealSheaf, exists_ideal_eq_span and exists_isFreeGenerator supply affine local generators b and corresponding module sections. ordAt_eq and ordAt_idealSheaf identify ord_P(b) with E(P).

For a nonzero rational function c on an open U with ord_P(c)+A(P)=0 at its closed points, prove that the constant rational section c freely generates O(A) on every smaller open. Injectivity follows from the embedding of regular sections in the function field. For surjectivity, local constancy on a nonempty integral open makes a section s constant. The quotient s/c has nonnegative orders at closed points by the defining bounds; at other points ord is zero by isClosed_of_coheight_eq_one and ord_eq_zero_of_coheight_neq_one. The already proved source theorem exists_germToFunctionField_eq_of_ord_nonneg then gives its regular-section representative. Treat zero sections separately; on the empty open both section modules are subsingletons. These are the fully proved private helper divisor_generator_of_orders and the existing source regular-section criterion, with no new assumed statement.

Apply the preceding criterion to each affine local generator b of the ideal product, with A=-D. This gives generators of O(-D). They have exactly the same transition relations as the ideal-module generators: applying sectionsι and germToFunctionField to a transition relation gives its equality in the rational functions, while divisor restriction and scalar multiplication have precisely these pointwise values. Glue with the source theorem Modules.nonempty_iso_of_isFreeGenerator to obtain I(E).toModules ≅ O(-D). Apply the same criterion to c=1,A=0 on the top open to prove O(0) ≅ O_C. These are the fully proved private helpers ideal_iso_negative and zero_divisor_iso_unit.

By [lem-sc-divisor-module-tensor-add], O(-D) tensor O(D) ≅ O(0). Compose with the two preceding isomorphisms to get I(E) tensor O(D) ≅ O_C. By [lem-sc-invertible-dual], I(E) tensor I(E)^dual ≅ O_C. Insert the inverse of the first isomorphism to the left of I(E)^dual, associate, commute O(D) past I(E)^dual, then evaluate the ideal-dual pair and remove the tensor unit. This explicit composition yields I(E)^dual ≅ O(D). Rewrite I(E) as the product in the original statement.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $C$ a scheme smooth of relative dimension $1$ over
$k$.

1. Let $E=\sum_{i=1}^m n_i[P_i]$ be an effective divisor of $C$ (all
$n_i\ge0$), viewed as the effective Cartier divisor with ideal sheaf
$\mathcal{I}_E=\prod_i\mathcal{I}_{P_i}^{n_i}$. Then the class
$[\mathcal{O}_C(E)]\in\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ of [def-sc-divisor] equals the
class of the module $\mathcal{O}_C(E)=\mathcal{I}_E^\vee$ of
[def-pc-divisor-line-bundle].
1. If $C$ is moreover integral and Noetherian, every effective Cartier
divisor $D\subset C$ is of this form: with
$n_P=\operatorname{ord}_P(\mathcal{I}_D)$ the order of the ideal at the
closed point $P$ (only finitely many are nonzero) and $E=\sum_Pn_P[P]$, the
class $[\mathcal{O}_C(E)]$ of [def-sc-divisor] equals the class of
$\mathcal{I}_D^\vee$.

proof.text:
*(1).* Every local ring $\mathcal{O}_{C,P}$ at a closed point is regular of
dimension one ([lem-sc-smooth-regular]), hence a discrete valuation ring
([lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr]), and the ideal sheaf $\mathcal{I}_P$ of a
closed point is invertible ([lem-sc-point-cartier]). A product of
invertible ideal sheaves is invertible, and for invertible ideals
$\mathcal{I},\mathcal{J}$ multiplication
$\mathcal{I}\otimes\mathcal{J}\to\mathcal{I}\mathcal{J}$ is an isomorphism
(locally it sends $f\otimes g$ to $fg$ for local generators $f,g$, and $fg$
is again a non-zero-divisor). Hence
$[\mathcal{I}_E]=\prod_i[\mathcal{I}_{P_i}]^{n_i}$ in
$\operatorname{Pic}(C)$. Since the dual of an invertible module represents
the inverse class,

$$
[\mathcal{I}_E^\vee]=[\mathcal{I}_E]^{-1}=\prod_i[\mathcal{I}_{P_i}]^{-n_i}
=\prod_i[\mathcal{I}_{P_i}^\vee]^{n_i}=\prod_i[\mathcal{O}_C(P_i)]^{n_i},
$$

which is the class $[\mathcal{O}_C(E)]$ of [def-sc-divisor].

*(2).* By [lem-sc-cartier-divisor-points] the support of $D$ is a finite
set of closed points $P$, at which $\mathcal{I}_{D,P}=(t_P^{n_P})$ for a
uniformizer $t_P$ of the discrete valuation ring $\mathcal{O}_{C,P}$, with
$n_P=\operatorname{ord}_P(\mathcal{I}_D)\ge1$, and
$\mathcal{I}_{D,x}=\mathcal{O}_{C,x}$ at all other points. The ideal
$\mathcal{I}_E=\prod_P\mathcal{I}_P^{n_P}$ of $E=\sum_Pn_P[P]$ has the same
stalks, so $\mathcal{I}_D=\mathcal{I}_E$ (an ideal sheaf is determined by
its stalks), and (1) applies.
